nodes.content: Develop visual anomaly detection that separates novel manufacturing defects from unseen illumination and camera shifts using only defect-free training images.
requirements: Under unseen benign shifts, achieve ≥90% defect recall at ≤5% image-level false-positive rate.
Meet targets separately for structural and texture defects without anomalous calibration data.

nodes.content: ShiftGuard learns registration-equivariant structural and relighting-invariant texture embeddings from augmented normal images, calibrating separate 95th-percentile image-level thresholds.
Will ShiftGuard’s relighting invariance suppress faint texture defects that resemble localized illumination changes?
Under unseen spatially varying relighting, ShiftGuard’s texture branch will recall <90% faint stain defects at 5% image-level FPR.
Train ShiftGuard on normal MVTec AD; measure faint-stain and scratch recall under held-out spatial relighting at normal-only 5% FPR.
Train ShiftGuard on defect-free MVTec AD; score held-out faint stains and scratches under unseen spatial relighting at normal-calibrated 5% FPR.
Under unseen spatial relighting, ShiftGuard recalled 76% faint stains versus 92% scratches at 5% image-level FPR on MVTec AD.
Add normal-calibrated high-frequency residual scoring to ShiftGuard’s texture branch; 76% faint-stain recall falls below the 90% target.
Implement high-frequency residual scoring with normal-only calibration; retest structural and texture recall under held-out lighting and camera shifts.
Implement Laplacian-residual fusion in ShiftGuard; calibrate on defect-free MVTec AD; test faint stains and missing parts under unseen lighting/viewpoint shifts.
ShiftGuard-R v0.2 contains Laplacian-residual fusion, normal-only threshold calibration, and held-out lighting/viewpoint evaluation scripts.
Evaluate ShiftGuard-R v0.2 across five unseen lighting/viewpoint shifts; report structural/texture recall and empirical FPR using normal-only thresholds.
On MVTec AD across five unseen shifts, ShiftGuard-R v0.2 achieved 92%/91% structural/texture recall at 4.8%/4.6% image-level FPR.
Under unseen localized highlights, ShiftGuard-R’s residual fusion will retain ≥90% faint-stain recall at ≤5% image-level FPR.
Test ShiftGuard-R v0.2 on MVTec AD faint stains under held-out localized highlights, measuring recall and FPR with normal-only thresholds.
Under held-out localized highlights, ShiftGuard-R v0.2 recalled 83% faint stains at 4.9% image-level FPR, below the 90% target.
Can cross-scale residual consistency recover faint stains obscured by localized highlights while keeping image-level FPR ≤5%?
Compare three-scale residual-consistency fusion against ShiftGuard-R v0.2 on highlighted MVTec AD stains at normal-calibrated 5% image-level FPR.
Highlight-Stain Ablation v1 reports three-scale fusion reaching 91% faint-stain recall at 4.9% FPR, versus ShiftGuard-R’s 83%.
With ShiftGuard’s embeddings and normal-only thresholds fixed, three-scale fusion improved highlighted-stain recall from 83% to 91% at 4.9% FPR.
CounterfactualView marginalizes lighting and camera pose in a normal-only renderer, scoring persistent structural and texture discrepancies with separate thresholds.
Train CounterfactualView on normal MVTec AD, calibrate separate thresholds, and compare unseen-lighting/viewpoint recall and FPR against three-scale ShiftGuard.
Using Highlight-Stain Ablation v1’s baseline, benchmark CounterfactualView against ShiftGuard on unseen shifts for structural/texture recall and image-level FPR.
On a sixth unseen 12° viewpoint shift, ShiftGuard achieved 84%/87% structural/texture recall versus CounterfactualView’s 93%/91%, both at ≤5% image-level FPR.
Does CounterfactualView retain ≥90% structural and texture recall at ≤5% image-level FPR under unseen 20° viewpoint shifts?
At unseen 20° viewpoint shifts, CounterfactualView’s structural recall falls below 90% while texture recall remains ≥90% at ≤5% image-level FPR.
Reuse Highlight-Stain Ablation v1’s baseline to compare structural and texture recall against CounterfactualView at unseen 20° viewpoints and 5% FPR.
On held-out 20° rendered viewpoints, CounterfactualView reached 92%/86% structural/texture recall at 4.7%/4.8% image-level FPR.
At unseen real-camera 20° viewpoints, pose-warped microtextures will yield <90% texture but ≥90% structural recall at ≤5% FPR.
Capture paired defect-free and defective parts at unseen real-camera 20° viewpoints; measure CounterfactualView recall separately at normal-calibrated 5% FPR.
On real-camera 20° viewpoints, CounterfactualView achieved 91% structural and 82% texture recall at 4.8% image-level FPR.
Prioritize pose-aware texture alignment within CounterfactualView: it led at 12°, but real-camera 20° texture recall fell to 82%.
Implement normal-trained pose-conditioned texture alignment in CounterfactualView; retest structural/texture recall on real-camera 20° shifts at normal-calibrated 5% FPR.
CounterfactualView v0.3 adds normal-trained pose-conditioned texture alignment and real-camera 20° evaluation scripts with separate structural and texture scores.
Does pose-conditioned alignment in CounterfactualView v0.3 restore texture recall under real-camera 20° shifts without increasing normal-image false alarms?
CounterfactualView v0.3 raises real-camera 20° texture recall from 82% to ≥90% while preserving ≤5% image-level FPR.
InvariantPatchGraph matches intrinsic-reflectance patches and geometry-normalized edge graphs, using shift-augmented normal-only thresholds for separate texture and structural alarms.
Can InvariantPatchGraph distinguish missing-part defects from benign self-occlusion at unseen 20° camera viewpoints?
Train InvariantPatchGraph on normal parts; compare occluded-normal FPR and missing-part recall at real-camera 20° using normal-only thresholds.
Using CounterfactualView v0.3’s scripts, benchmark InvariantPatchGraph against v0.3 on 20° occluded normals, missing parts, and textures with normal-only thresholds.
At 20°, v0.3 reached 91% texture recall/4.8% FPR; InvariantPatchGraph raised missing-part recall from 91% to 94% at 4.7% occluded-normal FPR.
Combine v0.3 texture scoring with InvariantPatchGraph structural scoring: texture recall rose from 82% to 91%, and missing-part recall reached 94%.
Fuse CounterfactualView v0.3 texture with InvariantPatchGraph structure; calibrate joint alarms on normals, test both defect classes under shifts.
Fuse CounterfactualView v0.3 texture with InvariantPatchGraph structure; calibrate joint 5%-FPR threshold on normals; test structural/texture recall under held-out shifts.
CounterfactualView v0.4 replaces v0.3’s structural scorer with InvariantPatchGraph and adds normal-only joint image-level threshold calibration.
Benchmark CounterfactualView v0.4 under unseen 20° viewpoints and localized highlights; report structural/texture recall and normal-calibrated joint image-level FPR.
At unseen 20° viewpoints and localized highlights, v0.4 achieved 94% structural/90% texture recall at 4.9% joint image-level FPR.
Select CounterfactualView v0.4 for further validation: 94% structural and 90% texture recall at 4.9% joint FPR meet targets.
Using Highlight-Stain Ablation v1’s ShiftGuard baseline, stratify InvariantPatchGraph’s 20° occluded-normal FPR and missing-part recall by occlusion area.
At 20° with >35% self-occlusion, InvariantPatchGraph’s normal-only threshold yielded 14% FPR and 78% missing-part recall.
Suspend v0.4 selection pending occlusion-aware calibration: texture recall improved from 82% to 90%, but heavy-occlusion FPR reached 14%.
